For almost four decades, I've been sitting on a story about New York Senator
Chuck Schumer that shines a light on his penchant for self-serving, misleading
exaggeration.

I only tell it now because I have been reminded of this character flaw in the
way Schumer is boasting of the credit due him for Democrats taking control of
the U.S. Senate in the midterm elections, as he runs for majority leader.

Back in 1988, I was part of Rev. Jesse Jackson's team negotiating the
Democratic Party's platform with Gov. Michael Dukakis's representatives at
that year's national convention. The Dukakis campaign was willing to
compromise on a few of the platform planks we were proposing, but refused to
give any ground on language we sought referring to Palestinian rights.

Our minority plank on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict was quite modest,
calling for "Mutual recognition, territorial compromise, and self-
determination for both peoples." Despite our efforts to offer further
concessions, the Dukakis team was adamant in their rejection - at one point
telling me, "If the 'p word' is even mentioned at the convention, you'll be
responsible for destroying the Democratic Party."
